newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sleepy Mexico peso ends mixed on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Sleepy Mexico peso ends mixed on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso MXAAA closed mixed on Friday due to swaps after what traders said was a quiet session.
"It was a quiet session, with the peso buoyed in some contracts by demand for pesos to invest in the money market over the weekend," said a trader.

Traders tended to sell dollars in the same-day market and buy them back at 24 hours. The advantage of 24-hour contracts is that they do not need to be paid for until Monday, and with pesos that can meanwhile be invested in fixed-income instruments.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.7 of a centavo firmer at 7.8940/7.9010, while the 24-hour currency closed 0.1 of a centavo weaker at 7.8910/7.8930.
The same-day peso had closed earlier one centavo weaker at 7.8930/7.8870 per dollar.
Traders said one reason for calm prevailing in the session was that many dealers were travelling to a convention on futures in the Caribbean resort of Cancn.
Another reason for calm trading was the Federal Open Market Committee's decision on Wednesday not to raise U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
They added that economic decisions weighed more heavily than political ones in foreign exchange trading.

"The peso is holding steady, despite the PRI's decision to go it alone in the political reform debate," said a trader, referring to Thursday's decision by ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) deputies in Congress to water down political reforms set out in a bill drafted after two years of multiparty talks.
The 48-hour peso closed the week 1.1 centavos firmer than at last week's close of 7.9060/7.9120.
Traders expected dealings to be quiet again next week, due to a holiday Wednesday marking the anniversary of the Mexican Revolution.
